newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: MCI eases as NZ debt market plays chicken with RB.
newsitem.headline: MCI eases as NZ debt market plays chicken with RB.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.10 PCT (PREV 8.10) US 5-YR 6.11 (PREV 6.07) NZD/USD 0.6421/28 (PREV 0.6433/40) US 10-YR 6.22 (PREV 6.18)
New Zealand monetary conditions eased to over 100 basis points looser than the Reserve Bank wants on Tuesday morning as the market played chicken with the bank hours before key jobs data.
The Monetary Conditions Index fell to to 723 as the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index fell and the bank bills failed to adjust, with the bill futures actually rising a couple of points.
Dealers said the period before the jobs data due at 10.45 a.m. (2245 GMT) was a free time when the RB was highly unlikely to react.
As well, the market is anticipating the jobs data, particularly the rise in the hours worked, will be weaker than the RB's forecast and will justify a further easing.

The RB forecasts that the critical hours worked number will show a rise of 1.9 percent in the June quarter while market expectations are for a 1.0-1.5 percent rise. A number in line with the bank's will see a hefty sell off in the bills.
Economists pick unemployment will rise to 6.9 percent from 6.4 percent.
